objectives: Use Lesson 77 evidence to select a weak /f/ component.
Provide targeted remediation for recognition, decoding, encoding, comprehension, or fluency.
Measure transfer using fresh reassessment items.
Apply an explicit advance or reteach decision.
concepts: Remediation must match the diagnosed weakness.
Fresh items provide stronger evidence of transfer.
Mastery requires adequate overall performance without a critical component gap.

definitions.definition: Instruction focused on the specific skill component identified as weak.
A follow-up check using unseen items measuring the same target.
A defined performance threshold used to decide whether a learner progresses.

workedExamples: Encoding gap → phoneme segmentation and spelling.
commonMistakes: Remediating every component when only one is weak.
Advancing despite a critical weak component.
Increasing speed before accuracy is secure.

basic: Review the weakest /f/ component with controlled examples.
conceptual: Match common errors to the appropriate remediation path.
application: Apply targeted /f/ repair and interpret reassessment evidence.
higherOrderThinking: Explain why mastery must include both accuracy and component stability.
mixedReview: Combine all /f/ components in fresh transfer tasks.

mistakeBasedRevision: If one critical component remains below target, reteach that component.
weakTopicRevision: Repeat the lowest-performing /f/ component with new controlled items.

activities.name: Advance or reteach
steps: Reteach the specific gap when it is not met.

scoring.method: component-level accuracy with overall mastery gate

decisionRules.advance: Advance when reassessment reaches 0.8 and no critical component remains below target.
decisionRules.reteach: Reteach the specific component when performance remains below 0.8.

outcomes: Learner demonstrates transfer on fresh /f/ items.
System routes the learner to progression or additional remediation.

Which happens first: Finn gets the fan, or Finn puts it on the mat?
